tier_reason: First-party table in docs/source/benchmarks.md shows FlatBuffers (binary) vs Protocol Buffers LITE: Decode+Traverse+Dealloc 0.08 s vs 302 s and Encode 3.2 s vs 185 s per 1M iterations, 'running on Windows 7 64bit' with no compiler, flags, or CPU model. The >50x gain with unstated flags also triggers the cap at C.

corrections.caveats: The benchmark text says only 'running on Windows 7 64bit' (no compiler, flags, or CPU model) and is clearly old (Windows 7 / VS2010 era). The >3000x decode ratio is implausible for two optimized libraries and most likely reflects a debug or unoptimized protobuf build, so it is capped at tier C under the >50x-implausible rule. The doc says the benchmark code lives in a git branch named `benchmarks`, but that branch no longer exists (GitHub API 404). The current master benchmarks/cpp/ directory only has FlatBuffers and raw-struct benches and no protobuf comparison, so the code behind these protobuf numbers is not publicly reproducible today.

notes: Numbers and derived ratios match the page (302/0.08 = 3775x, 185/3.2 = 57.8x). Metadata checks out: Apache-2.0, not a fork, not archived, 26,494 stars, last commit 2026-09-14 (active). The only change is to caveats, which now say the referenced `benchmarks` branch is gone.

tier_reason: Upgraded from D to C. The author's announcement post on the Vitess blog (Vicent Marti, 2021-06-03) gives profiled unmarshal overhead for a VReplication stress test: 7.17 CPU s with stock APIv2 protoc-gen-go code, 4.15 CPU s with vtprotobuf, and 0.63 CPU s with vtprotobuf plus memory pooling. These are first-party numbers with no hardware, Go version, or benchmark code, so tier C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Unmarshal overhead in a VReplication stress test: 7.17 CPU s (ProtoBuf APIv2, stock protoc-gen-go) vs 4.15 CPU s (APIv2 + vtprotobuf), ~1.7x (derived from page data); with vtprotobuf memory pooling 0.63 CPU s, ~11.4x (derived from page data). For reference, the page gives APIv1 at 7.47 CPU s and APIv1 + gogo at 4.24 CPU s.
corrections.workload: Profiled CPU time spent in Protobuf unmarshaling during a synthetic Vitess VReplication stress test that fully replicates a large MySQL table between keyspaces; compares Go code generated by the stock protoc-gen-go (APIv2), gogo (APIv1), and vtprotobuf's UnmarshalVT helpers with and without the generated memory pools
corrections.caveats: The numbers come from the author's own 2021 announcement post on the Vitess blog. They are a single workload-specific profile (VReplication row streaming) with no hardware, Go version, or linked benchmark code, and the repo contains no benchmark directory. The ~11x figure depends on memory pooling, where the application reuses Response objects, and is not a pure codegen win. The pure codegen gain is ~1.7x. Upstream google.golang.org/protobuf may have narrowed the gap since 2021.

notes: The record had no benchmark page. The author's Vitess blog post has real numbers against the stock Go protobuf generator, so the tier goes up from D to C. Metadata checks out: BSD-3-Clause, not a fork, not archived, 1118 stars, last commit 2026-07-02 (active). The 'metric' field (currently 'other', which is really CPU time) is not in the allowed corrections list, so it was left alone.
